text: The ForEach activity defines a repeating control flow, exactly like a foreach loop in any programming language. Give it a real collection, and it runs its child activities once for every single item inside that collection, start to finish.

ForEach needs an actual array to iterate over — often an array-type variable defined right on the pipeline itself, or just as commonly, a Lookup activity's own output with firstRowOnly set to false, exactly like Lesson 14 already covered.

Drag ForEach onto the canvas, then select the Items field and choose Add dynamic content to reference that array directly. Sequential and Batch count, right alongside it, control exactly how the loop actually runs underneath.

Inside any activity nested inside the loop, reference whatever it's currently iterating over with item, in parentheses. If Items is one, two, three, item returns one on the first pass, two on the second, three on the third — exactly the pattern a Copy activity uses to reference whichever table a given iteration is actually handling.

Sequential true runs iterations one at a time, in order, genuinely safe by default. Sequential false runs them in parallel instead, up to fifty at once, controlled by batch count — faster, but use real caution: if two concurrent iterations write to the exact same file or the exact same variable, you can end up with a genuine conflict.

One real limit worth remembering: a ForEach can't directly contain another ForEach or an Until — the workaround is a two-level pipeline, an outer loop calling an Execute Pipeline activity for the inner one. Next: the Until activity — looping until a condition is genuinely true, instead of over a fixed collection.
